name: Mannequin Pussy
label: Epitaph
lede: Marisa Dabice and Athanasios Paul started Mannequin Pussy as a two-piece in Connecticut, and fourteen years later Pitchfork gave the band's fourth album an 8.8 and Best New Music.

eras.title: Two friends, a pile of cassettes, then Philadelphia
eras.text: Dabice and Paul put out EPs called Bonerjamz! and Meatslave and learn the DIY circuit on cassettes. By 2013 Dabice lives in Philadelphia, and the duo has a drummer and a first album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy · Crack Magazine · Philadelphia Inquirer
years.h: Two friends from school start a band in Connecticut
years.p: Marisa "Missy" Dabice sang and played guitar; Athanasios Paul played drums. Crack places the start in Connecticut.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band to October 2010 and says Dabice and Paul met in school. Crack Magazine puts the early band in Connecticut, before the move to Philadelphia.

The Inquirer says the band as it is known today took shape in 2013, shortly before Dabice relocated, which is why some profiles give 2013 as the start.

years.cap: Mannequin Pussy at DBA, Brooklyn, July 5, 2011
years.h: Bonerjamz! and Meatslave both come out in 2011
years.p: The first two EPs, from a duo still working out what it was, with Dabice on guitar and vocals and Paul on drums.

years.h: Trash Palace Tapes puts out a split with Idaho's Art Fad
years.p: Banditos is a tour tape and carries thirteen of the band's songs. The same month, "Clue Juice" lands on Leisure Rules, a Reeks Of Effort cassette comp.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists both July 2012 tape releases: the Art Fad split, with thirteen Mannequin Pussy songs on it, and the Reeks Of Effort compilation that carried "Clue Juice".

years.h: Drew Adler takes the drum stool, Paul moves to guitar
years.p: The duo turns into a proper band: Drew Adler behind the kit, Paul on guitar, Dabice out front.

years.cap: Mannequin Pussy at Big Snow, January 21, 2013
years.h: The Rotunda pays $100, the most they had ever made
years.p: Dabice had moved to Philadelphia after meeting players like Nicole Snyder and Rachel Gagliardi of [[Slutever|f8887032-74fc-4ce0-87df-963ab10b2629]] on tour. A West Philly room gave the band its first real night's pay.
years.xp: The Philadelphia Inquirer says Dabice left Connecticut after meeting women musicians including Snyder and Gagliardi while touring. It describes a 2013 show at the Rotunda in West Philadelphia that paid the band $100, "the most money we had ever made."

years.h: Gypsy Pervert comes out on cassette only
years.p: A limited run on Rarebit Records, a little over eighteen minutes of noise, melody and shouting.

eras.title: Gypsy Pervert becomes Mannequin Pussy
eras.text: A label deal, a new title for the debut and a new rhythm section. By the end of 2016 the band has the lineup and the songs that get it noticed outside Philadelphia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy (album) · Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy · Crack Magazine
years.h: Gypsy Pervert becomes Mannequin Pussy on Tiny Engines
years.p: The band worried the original title read as a slur against Romani people, so the September 2014 reissue went out under the band's own name.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the album was retitled when the band signed to Tiny Engines in 2014, because of concerns about the original title's pejorative connotations toward Romani people. The September 9, 2014 release was a co-release between Rarebit Records and Tiny Engines; the band produced it with D. A. Stern.

Crack describes the record as minute-long hardcore jams. Frank Valish of Under the Radar wrote that the songs "hit you over the head like an anvil" while holding girl-group melodies and shoegaze haze.

years.h: Kaleen Reading takes over the drums, and stays
years.p: [[Kaleen Reading|2c1636c7-37e0-459c-a64e-3d28f0343d32]] replaces Adler and is still the band's drummer a decade later.

years.h: Bear Regisford brings a bass and a second voice
years.p: Colins "Bear" Regisford makes it a four-piece with Dabice, Paul and Reading, and the band leans on his vocals from then on.

years.h: Romantic puts hardcore speed and pop hooks in one song
years.p: Tracked at Big Mamas Recording in Philadelphia and mixed by the band itself, it runs seventeen minutes.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave Romantic 7.6 and The A.V. Club an A-minus, per Wikipedia. Rolling Stone ranked the title track No. 14 on its 50 best songs of 2016, and Stereogum made the album its album of the week.

Dabice has said the songs came from two years of working through depression and anxiety and finding out she was not alone in it.

eras.title: Patience pays off
eras.text: Touring hard, videos with a point of view, and an Epitaph deal. Patience gets an 8.4 from Pitchfork in 2019, and "Drunk II" lands at No. 16 on its list of the year's best songs.

years.h: Audiotree records the four-piece live
years.p: A live session for Audiotree with Dabice, Paul, Reading and Regisford.

years.h: The "Pledge" video follows a woman who stops taking orders
years.p: Dabice told DIY the clip tracks a woman whose movements are dictated by a man and the people around her, until she makes a declaration to herself.
years.xp: The video went up on YouTube on May 30, 2017. Dabice's description to DIY magazine was of a woman whose movements are controlled by a man and by those around her, and of the declaration she is able to make once she frees herself.

years.cap: Dabice, Paul and Regisford on the Patience tour, September 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Patience (Mannequin Pussy album) · Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy · The Ringer
years.h: Patience arrives on Epitaph and Pitchfork gives it an 8.4
years.p: Recorded at Studio 4 in Conshohocken with [[Will Yip|282e2957-fd09-4260-babf-50f1d57eeb75]] and released June 21, it runs 25 minutes. Pitchfork put it at No. 35 on its best albums of 2019.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Quinn Moreland called Patience one of the best punk rock records of 2019, per Wikipedia. "Drunk II" was No. 16 on Pitchfork's 100 best songs of 2019, and in 2026 Rolling Stone ranked the album No. 42 on its 100 greatest punk albums.

Dabice's own summary of the theme was un-learning self-hatred and being patient with yourself and others. Wikipedia dates the Epitaph signing to 2019; The Ringer puts it after Romantic in 2016 (see questions).

years.h: "Cream" goes 1970s horror, days before Patience
years.p: Director Hanna Hamilton took her cues from 1970s horror films for the clip.

years.h: Tiny Engines, the band's old label, goes on hiatus
years.p: Accounting disputes over unpaid artist royalties stop the label that released the band's 2014 and 2016 albums.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the pause and says it affected Mannequin Pussy. The band later bought back its masters (see 2022) and started its own imprint.

eras.title: Stolen vans, HBO and one founder out
eras.text: A pandemic cancels a tour, a van is stolen twice and two Mannequin Pussy songs end up in an HBO murder mystery. Paul leaves after eleven years, and the founding duo is down to one.

years.h: The pandemic cancels the Best Coast tour
years.p: Touring paid the bills, and Dabice later said the band lost its main form of income and some of its biggest opportunities.
years.xp:
Crack reports the March 2020 Best Coast tour was halted by the pandemic. During the shutdown the van was broken into in Philadelphia and its catalytic converter taken; when Regisford went to file a police report he learned the whole van had been stolen. It was found dumped across town three days later.

Dabice told Guitar.com the band "lost our main form of income."

years.h: After eleven years, Paul leaves
years.p: The founding guitarist is going "to begin a new chapter in his life," and Dabice, Reading and Regisford carry on as a three-piece.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives March 18, 2021 for the announcement. Crack says Paul left in early 2020, so the date conflicts (see questions).

years.h: Dabice turns up as an FBI agent in a Japanese Breakfast video
years.p: The cameo is in the clip for "Be Sweet," a single from [[Japanese Breakfast|8c529495-91f5-4e2f-b71b-adcb66878d04]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect (Mannequin Pussy EP) · Crack Magazine
years.h: Will Yip gets the band back in the room for Perfect
years.p: It was the first time the band walked into the studio without pre-written songs, and all five were finished in two days. Pitchfork's Arielle Gordon gave it 7.2.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the EP was recorded between August 2020 and February 2021. Crack reports it was tracked at Studio 4 in Conshohocken after months without in-person contact, and that all five songs were done in two days.

years.h: A made-up band on Mare of Easttown plays their songs
years.p: "Who You Are" and "In Love Again" are performed by Androgynous, the miniseries' fictional band, and Dabice later said the placement gave Mannequin Pussy "cultural and artistic legitimacy."
years.xp: The Philadelphia Inquirer credits HBO's Mare of Easttown (2021) with that legitimacy, in Dabice's words. The show is set in suburban Pennsylvania.

years.big: Even if they hate it, they're calling it perfect.
years.src: Crack Magazine · Wikipedia: Perfect (Mannequin Pussy EP)
years.h: Dabice names the EP Perfect for the people who'll hate it
years.p: Her explanation of the title, quoted in Crack.
years.xp: Crack Magazine quotes Dabice on the title as a reply to people who will pick the record apart. Wikipedia lists Clash at 8 and a Metacritic score of 80.

years.h: Thieves take the van, the trailer and $50,000 of gear in Akron
years.p: The Ford Econoline and trailer disappeared during the tour, and the band played its remaining dates on borrowed gear.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the theft on October 30, 2021 and values the equipment at more than $50,000. The same month the band added [[Carolyn Haynes|5a7b8fb2-ce81-43c1-90f8-b1257f45af63]] (guitar, keyboards) and [[Maxine Steen|74a4fb47-9fde-49ea-8c6d-3523b1254b0d]] (guitar) as touring members.

hate5six filmed the band's full show at Union Transfer in Philadelphia in October 2021, days after the gear went missing.

eras.title: A label of their own, and an 8.8
eras.text: The band buys back its early records, starts Romantic Records and, with John Congleton in Los Angeles, makes the album Pitchfork ranks No. 11 of 2024.

years.h: The band buys its masters back from Tiny Engines
years.p: It paid for the rights to Romantic, the 2016 record the label had released.
years.xp: Guitar.com dates the buyback to the year before its August 2023 announcement; Wikipedia places the buyback in August 2023 alongside the label launch (see questions).

years.h: Romantic Records opens with Romantic on vinyl
years.p: The band's own imprint starts with a limited reissue of the out-of-print 2016 album, and thanks Tiny Engines for being among its first supporters.

years.h: Maxine Steen goes from hired guitarist to full member
years.p: After two years on tour with the band, [[Maxine Steen|74a4fb47-9fde-49ea-8c6d-3523b1254b0d]] becomes the fourth member and restores the four-piece.

years.h: "I Got Heaven" arrives nine months early, shot on a farm
years.p: The title track came out August 28, 2023, with a video by Mason Mercer and Anthony Miralles.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Got Heaven · GRAMMY.com · The Ringer · Philadelphia Inquirer
years.h: Pitchfork calls I Got Heaven Best New Music with an 8.8
years.p: Released March 1 on Epitaph and produced by John Congleton in Los Angeles, the fourth album is the band's first made outside Philadelphia. Pitchfork later put it at No. 11 for 2024.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia's reception box, Pitchfork gave the record 8.8 and Best New Music; Metacritic scored it 89. Exclaim! put it No. 6 and The Ringer named it the No. 2 album of 2024 and Mannequin Pussy its band of the year. The Ringer says Pitchfork later ranked it 87th among the best albums of the 2020s.

Congleton came through Epitaph founder Brett Gurewitz. Dabice told GRAMMY.com the songs grew out of two years off from dating after three members' breakups at once, and that "Split Me Open" came the day after a psychedelic trip at a family cabin in New Hampshire. "Loud Bark" opened the 2025 series The Hunting Wives, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The KEXP session: a full set in Seattle
years.p: The band plays the studio on the tour for I Got Heaven; KEXP recorded it July 11, 2024.

years.h: Dabice cancels the second European leg on a month's notice
years.p: She took nearly two months to recover. In October the band played the Best Friends Forever festival in Las Vegas.
years.xp:
The Ringer reports the band cancelled for its members' physical and mental wellbeing. Dabice said she "didn't want to be fucking seen by anyone," then spent nearly two months recovering with Pilates, energy healing and a music-industry therapist.

The Ringer also says the band at Best Friends Forever in October 2024 was "the most exciting, modern group of rock stars that anyone got to see."
